Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API baseline + multi-region pricing

Ben / Lauren — quick draft attached (draft_ratecard_v1.pdf). Notes:

- Recommended hosted token bands (hosted only, USD per 1k tokens):
  • 0 - 250M: $0.012 / 1k
  • 250M - 1B: $0.0098 / 1k
  • 1B - 5B: $0.0075 / 1k
  • 5B+: custom tier (negotiated, typically 10–20% below 1B-5B band).

- For mixed multi-region traffic we apply base price above + regional egress surcharge for EU of +5% to cover additional infra/replication costs. We can waive the surcharge on 24-month commitments >3B/mo.

- Rollover policy (proposal): unused committed tokens can roll over up to 25% of committed monthly amount, applied over the following 3 months. Rollover only on annual committed contracts (12+ months) and not for free trial credits.

- Dedicated recommendation: For predictable high sustained throughput (>=2B/mo steady), suggest a hybrid approach — Dedicated reservation for steady 1.2–1.5B tokens (sizable discount, typically additional 15–25% off hosted tiers) and hosted for burst/spikes. That reduces unit cost and preserves routing flexibility.

I attached a compact PDF with the rate bands and a sensitivity table (draft_ratecard_v1.pdf). Happy to tighten numbers for the pitch.

— Neha
Pricing & Revenue Ops

Attachment: draft_ratecard_v1.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API baseline + multi-region pricing

Agree with Neha's bands. A couple of tweaks to propose to Acme:

- Phased commitment (rower) — start with a 12-month term with a commitment floor (1.5B/mo). If they hit 2B for any quarter, we auto-escalate pricing to the next discount band and grant a one-time credits multiplier to offset the ramp month. This helps them avoid over-committing up front.

- Rollover clarity — allow up to 30% rollover on first-year commitments for 24-month deals, 20% for 12-month deals. We should keep a ceiling (6 months) on how long rollover can be applied.

- SLA / Multi-region — SLA remains the same but for multi-region + geo-redundancy we can offer a 99.95% composite uptime with a regional premium or a reduced premium if they accept eventual consistency for non-critical traffic.

- PoC credits — recommend offering a small PoC credit pool (equivalent to ~200M tokens) to validate latency/throughput across EU and NA. Makes procurement comfortable without affecting the committed baseline.

I'll draft the proposal language and outline the proposed 12 vs 24 month economics.

— Lauren
Head of Enterprise Sales Ops

Hi Sarah — thanks for the forecast. Attached is a consolidated proposal (ACME_Repricing_Proposal.pdf) that pulls in our hosted rate bands, proposed rollover mechanics, and a hybrid Dedicated-hosted path to optimize unit economics for your steady load + promotional spikes. High level:

- Hosted rate bands (per 1k tokens): 0-250M: $0.012 | 250M-1B: $0.0098 | 1B-5B: $0.0075
- EU surcharge: +5% on listed rates; waived for 24-month commitments >3B/mo
- Rollover: up to 25% monthly rollover for 12-month annualized commitments (30% for 24-month deals), apply over next 3 months; capped at 6 months of banked rollover credits.
- Hybrid recommendation: reserve Dedicated capacity for 1.2B steady tokens (15% additional discount on that portion) and keep hosted for burst. This materially reduces avg unit price for months with promotions.
- Terming: 12-month vs 24-month — 24-month offers deeper baseline reductions and full surcharge waiver at >3B/mo.
